title: Credit Builder Accounts Holding Limit and Reapplication Waits
content:
## Clause

1. A customer may hold 1 Credit Builder account at a time. The customer has no other Credit Builder account in applied or active status.
2. A customer whose earlier account was closed for delinquency may apply again only once the delinquency-closure wait (365 calendar days on every Credit Builder Accounts plan) has passed after that closing date, and after an early closure only once the plan's early-close wait has passed.

Both conditions are read from the customer's Credit Builder records: the status of each of the customer's Credit Builder accounts, and, for a closed account, its closing date and how it closed. The customer's statement about earlier accounts does not replace those records.

## Condition, judgement, result

| What the customer's Credit Builder records show | Judgement on a new Credit Builder application |
|---|---|
| another Credit Builder account in applied status | the one-account limit is not met |
| another Credit Builder account in active status | the one-account limit is not met |
| an earlier account closed for delinquency, the delinquency-closure wait not yet passed after its closing date | the customer may not apply again yet |
| an earlier account closed early, the plan's early-close wait not yet passed | the customer may not apply again yet |

The plan's early-close wait is the plan's figure for the calendar days after an early closure before a new Credit Builder application is taken. A plan whose wait is 0 days places no wait after an early closure.

## Points of judgement

- An account that matured, or an application that was cancelled, is in neither applied nor active status, so it does not count toward the one-account limit.
- The limit counts accounts across every Credit Builder Accounts plan: a customer with an active Credit Builder 600 Plan account holds the one account allowed, whichever plan the new application is for.
